correctness.rationale: An admissible extension is exactly an ideal L below x and a filter U above x with every l∈L below every u∈U. These conditions give transitivity; the generic poset extension property realizes each pattern and homogeneity over the fixed named base identifies precisely identical patterns. Pure lower or upper choices give twice the product of finite geometric sums minus the duplicated empty pattern. A mixed extension occurs in one chain and for grade j has j−1 splits into positive prefix and suffix lengths. The convolution for two chains gives coefficients 4j, 2a+j+1, and 2(a+b−j+1) on the three stated intervals. The final jump always decreases; the only valley occurs for a≥3 and b≥a+2, with 4a>3a+2<3a+3. Log-concavity holds for a=1 by the affine middle range and its boundary inequalities, and by direct calculation for (2,2) and (2,3). The (8,8,9) triple rules out a=2,b≥4; for a≥3 the valley rules out b≥a+2 and the specified boundary triples for b=a and b=a+1 have excess of neighbor product over middle square 4a(a−2) and 2(a−2)(a+1), respectively. A fresh exact census independently enumerated the 3^n assignments of each named point below, above or incomparable to x and tested transitivity for all 66 integer-partition profiles for 1≤n≤8 (187,374 assignments). It matched the formula throughout and reproduced precisely the asserted first failure profiles and all three displayed coefficient lists. Finally (3,n−3) and (2,n−2) keep the same failing triples at every size in their respective ranges.

value.rationale: Disjoint chains provide a natural test of whether one-point comparability grades inherit the usual coefficient shape of the convolution of chain polynomials. The proof identifies precisely how mixed extensions change the answer for two chains and separates first loss of log-concavity from first loss of unimodality over all profiles. The smallest obstructions and persistence provide explicit tests for any proposed general shape theorem, beyond either the already-shared formula or an isolated coefficient example.
residual_risks: Does not give an unrestricted shape theorem for three or more unequal chains or arbitrary posets.
